extracted.intended_audience: general readers and biographers interested in 19th-century American theatre and the life of Edwin Forrest
extracted.subtask_description: A biographical narrative of the 19th-century American actor Edwin Forrest, intended to document his life, character, career, family background, and historical significance, using documentary evidence and personal testimony. The work emphasizes a stage-centered perspective while aiming for candid, balanced, and historically useful treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness / No whitewashing
rubrics_metrics.description: Forrest's request: "Tell the truth frankly. Let there be no whitewashing. Show me just as I have been and am."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author pledges to "use no disguising varnish, but let the facts stand forth." Will spare no pains to learn the truth, neither holding back nor trimming down foibles and vices nor magnifying virtues; ready to bear censure if the whole truth is told.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of primary sources and broad documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The author lists sources: (1) conversations and correspondence, for five years, with Forrest himself; (2) conversations and correspondence with his chief friends and intimates; (3) half a dozen biographical sketches (some printed, some manuscript); (4) magazine articles and newspaper notices and criticisms (some twenty thousand); (5) the mass of letters and papers left by him at his death, made available by his executors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on a wide and concrete evidentiary base—personal interviews, private correspondence, contemporaneous press coverage, existing sketches, and the subject's own papers—to establish facts and support claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance and impartial criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: The book will be written "from that popularized academic or philosophic point of view which surveys the whole field of human life in a spirit at once of scientific appreciation, poetic sympathy, and impartial criticism."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for an even-handed tone: combine sympathetic understanding with critical distance; present both virtues and faults; expose the 'ill side' as frankly as the 'good side' and point moral lessons without partisan bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage-centered perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: "The work will be written more from the stage point of view than from the pulpit point of view."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize the subject's professional life as an actor—training, public performance, art and technique—while still situating him within larger social and moral contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide concrete illustrations to support claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Author uses "two definite illustrations" (e.g., refuting charges of quarrelsomeness and pecuniary meanness) to show that statements are strict and literal truth rather than vague generalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support general assertions about character or reputation with specific incidents, documented facts, and illustrative episodes drawn from primary sources and press accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim to vindicate or correct the public record where warranted
rubrics_metrics.description: Forrest "has a claim for posthumous justice as one who was wronged in important particulars of his life and misjudged in essential elements of his character... It seems due to justice that the facts be stated, and his character vindicated."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate alleged misrepresentations; set out evidence to correct common misconceptions; present countervailing facts when public judgment appears inverted or unfair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect subject's stated wishes and quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Forrest's expressed desire that the truth be told and his quoting of Bannister's memoirs are recorded and used by the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate the subject's own voice and requests (quotations and stated preferences) where available; use them to frame the biographical approach while still applying independent verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize the life historically and nationally
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative situates Forrest's life within sweeping American changes (1806–1872), noting expansion of states, population growth, and shifts in national literary and civic life; also treats his "strictly American character."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate the subject's personal story to broader national, cultural, and historical developments so the biography illuminates larger themes and social transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include genealogical and family background
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed attention to parentage and family (father William Forrest, mother Rebecca Lauman), ancestry, family coat of arms, children's fates, and family influences on character and opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace family origins, upbringing, siblings' lives, and early domestic circumstances as necessary materials for understanding formation of character and career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select subjects of instructive public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: "The composition of a narrative doing justice to a life with such contents and such relations may well be thought worth the while... the result cannot fail to offer instructions worthy the attention of the American people."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose biographical subjects whose lives throw light on civic, artistic, or moral questions of public concern so the biography has instructive as well as anecdotal value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid undue laudation; invite candid reader judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Author asks readers not to assume a tendency to undue laudation and requests "that a candid examination be given to the evidence he adduces, and then that a corresponding decision be rendered."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present evidence transparently and allow readers to form judgments rather than relying on hagiography or defensive praise; explicitly acknowledge limitations of evidence when present.
